subject: general
question:
The figure given below shows the sectional view of the human female reproductive system. Identify the option stating correct functions of the labelled parts A and B.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b124e6a05594ce214b6e36ff2bb5087f1873f856afbff1879886ee20527306f2.png]

options.text: A - Implantation and development of embryo, B - Fertilisation of egg
Fertilisation of egg, B - Implantation and development of embryo
A - Formation of egg, B - Fertilisation of egg
A - Fertilisation of egg, B - Formation of egg

solution:
The correct answer is **A - Implantation and development of embryo, B - Fertilisation of egg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​Human fertilization is the joining of a human egg and sperm, which mainly takes place in the fallopian tube's ampulla.
 
• The outcome of this union results in the creation of a fertilized egg known as a zygote, which starts the embryonic development process.
 
• When a blastocyst develops into an embryo and attaches to the uterine wall, it has reached the stage of development known as implantation in mammals.
 
• When the first stage of gestation, implantation is successful, the female is regarded as pregnant.
 
• In the human uterus, the implantation location is often in the upper and posterior wall in the midsagittal plane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Humans reproduce sexually, in which the male and female gametes fertilise to create an embryo. Internal fertilisation, which occurs inside a female's body, is the process by which human embryos are fertilised.
 
• The formation and growth of the human embryo are known as human embryonic development or human embryogenesis.
 
• Human embryogenesis is distinguished by the embryo's early development phases of cell division and cellular differentiation.
 
• In a human, the first eight weeks of development after fertilisation are known as embryonic development, and at the start of the ninth week, the embryo is referred to as a foetus.
